# Lean formalization orchestrator

Read the repository's agent instructions, orchestration rules, plan, and active
ledgers before acting. Keep the process small enough that the author can inspect
and operate it. If an author has selected the frozen-anchor workflow below but a
repository policy still imposes a blanket zero-`sorry` development rule, treat
that as a policy mismatch to amend before graph extraction; do not silently
abandon statement freezing.

## Freeze keystone statements; only proofs may be provisional

The mathematical interface is the actual Lean declaration. A Markdown note,
“contract,” candidate declaration, tracked scratch probe, intended API,
placeholder type/body, convenience specialization, or promise of later
characterization is not formalization. It may not be approved, manifested,
frozen, used as a graph anchor, consumed by a proof, or counted as progress.

Before author approval, every theorem type and every definition type and body
must be the exact intended final declaration, with its real source carriers,
binders, quantifier order, and imports. A transient untracked file may check
that this exact command elaborates; delete it after use. Do not commit a
candidate or probe.

Once the author approves an exact keystone proposition or theorem, freeze it
immediately with the manifest-bound body `by sorry` and state `DRAFT_SORRY`.
Do not postpone the freeze until its proof is known: that recreates the
statement-drift failure this workflow is designed to prevent. The statement is
already final. It is `FROZEN_UNPROVED`, cannot satisfy a proved dependency, and
cannot be imported by production/provider code. Definitions neither contain
nor depend on this exception.

Every draft exception must be the sole public declaration in its frozen file
and have a unique manifest entry recording its source/version, exact export,
declaration/ABI hash, provider, exact allowed body, quarantine, and
`DRAFT_SORRY` state. All unmanifested `sorry`, `admit`, custom axioms,
placeholder definitions, and conclusion-shaped hypotheses remain forbidden.

A genuine predicate defined by the source, such as an induction state, may be a
literal `def : Prop`. A theorem-shaped predicate, standing-assumption package,
result bundle, or generic “input/bridge/consequence” interface may not replace a
source theorem.

## Admit definitions by their mathematics

A definition must already mean the source object on its whole public carrier.
Reject fallback zero/default branches, valid-locus-only semantics, arbitrary
witness choices, over-broad carriers with invented off-source behavior, and
reconstruction formulas whose equivalence to the source is promised for later.

When the source defines an object as the unique object satisfying a property:

1. write the exact well-definedness theorem (`exists`/`existsUnique`) using the
   real source carriers;
2. obtain independent source/binder/semantics review and author approval of its
   exact Lean type;
3. freeze it as a theorem [other project redacted], then prove, seal, and audit it;
4. only after that proof is available, write the final definition from it; and
5. land the definition with a separately named, sorry-free theorem asserting
   the complete source characterization and uniqueness.

The well-definedness theorem may contain only source premises, standing
assumptions, typing data, and explicit author rulings. Response existence,
integrability, linearity, quadraticity, symmetry, representability, and other
steps needed to prove it are graph dependencies, never binders. Once uniqueness
is proved, Classical.choose from that ∃! is legitimate; choosing from mere
existence or a non-unique family is forbidden.

The definition and characterization are one semantic unit, even when the
one-declaration-per-file rule puts them in separate files. Review and version
them together, give each a manifest entry, and land them in the same commit.
Every downstream graph node and proof depends on the
characterization theorem, not merely on the definition's codomain. If the
source instead gives a literal formula or predicate, audit and freeze that
literal body; do not invent an existence theorem merely for ceremony.

## Freeze the source-facing declarations

Do this before extracting their proof graph or assigning downstream proof work.

1. Select a small constitutional surface: main roots, subsection/induction
   gates, and definitions whose meaning changes them. Do not freeze every
   helper lemma.
2. Transcribe each target from a pinned source and approved errata. Record
   source ranges, premises, conclusion, quantifier order, constant/witness
   scope, split decisions, and unresolved questions. These notes are evidence,
   not a substitute declaration. Old Lean and old graphs are mining evidence
   only after this source pass.
3. Resolve every meaning-carrying Lean definition and carrier. Expand bundled
   assumptions and typeclass inputs far enough to expose their logical content.
4. Elaborate the exact final command transiently, then have a reviewer who did
   not write it compare that command directly with the source. Reject the first
   premise, field, fallback, or semantic choice not justified by source data,
   standing assumptions, typing, or an explicit author ruling.
5. Show the author the complete exact declaration: imports, explicit/implicit/
   instance binders, result, and a definition's whole body. Approval of a topic
   or prose summary is not approval of unseen Lean code.
6. After approval, place one public declaration in one frozen Lean file and add
   exactly one project-owned manifest entry binding its source, path, fully
   qualified export, provider identity when applicable, frozen bytes, and
   state. Every frozen Lean file must have exactly one manifest owner.

A source theorem may be split only when the author approves the split. Preserve
a shared constant or witness in one joint declaration unless the author
explicitly permits independent choices.

## Build the source dependency graph

Build the graph only after its root declarations are actual approved anchors.

- Give each source theorem, substantive proof step, and external input a stable
  node ID and line-addressable source range.
- Point roots at exact manifest entries and frozen exports.
- Treat every edge as an obligation to prove and consume a result. It is never
  permission to copy a predecessor's conclusion into a hypothesis.
- Route uses of a source-characterized definition through its proved
  characterization theorem.
- Review topology independently for omissions, circles, wrong edge direction,
  hidden external inputs, undischarged conditional premises, and false
  parallelism.
- Keep proof status separate from topology; never infer proof from a file's
  existence or compilation alone.

Assign work from the dependency-ready frontier. Off-frontier work needs a
recorded reason, such as source-faithful infrastructure needed by several
nodes.

## Prove below the anchors

Providers are ordinary Lean modules below frozen declarations in the import
DAG. They prove the exact target from graph predecessors and approved external
inputs; they never import a draft target. While an anchor remains DRAFT_SORRY, its
registered provider module/export is also quarantined from every module except
the provider itself and that frozen anchor. Otherwise production could bypass
the frozen audit by importing the implementation theorem directly.

For each worker:

- give one bounded target, exact source/anchor identity, owned files, allowed
  dependencies, validation command, stop condition, and handoff format;
- repeat repository hard rules verbatim when required;
- forbid edits to frozen declarations and extra source-facing premises;
- require the worker to stop if the exact API is insufficient; and
- allow conditional internal helpers only under distinct names, never as a
  source theorem or a closed graph node.

Use subagents for independent, non-overlapping work. Keep source interpretation,
shared APIs, and decisions affecting several packets with the orchestrator.
Review every diff and run the relevant checks; do not infer success from a
worker's prose report.

## Seal and audit

Seal a theorem by changing only its registered proof body to a short exact
assembly such as:

```lean
by exact Project.Provider.result
```

Then run the project checker, compile the frozen export, inspect its axioms,
and obtain an independent audit. Mark it `PROVED` only when all pass.

The audit must verify:

- the frozen export and bytes match the author-approved code;
- source ranges and every binder/quantifier match the source and rulings;
- every meaning-carrying definition, carrier, normalization, and source watch
  item is faithful;
- no hard proof step is an explicit, implicit, instance, or bundled hypothesis;
- the provider actually consumes the intended predecessors;
- every conditional premise is discharged at each application; and
- project-owned declarations contain no unauthorized `sorryAx` or custom axiom.

Compilation is not a fidelity verdict. One extra premise fails as decisively as
sixty-five. A producer for that premise does not repair the frozen statement;
the producer belongs inside its proof.

If an approved declaration is wrong, stop. Obtain an author ruling, create a
versioned successor, re-anchor the graph, and invalidate dependent proof/audit
status. Never repair a frozen declaration in place for proof convenience.

## Lean module system (mandatory)

Every regular `.lean` file in a campaign is a Lean module. This is standard
from 2026-09-29. Palomar rejects any submission containing a non-module file,
and a module cannot import a non-module file.

- **At planning.** Confirm that the toolchain, Mathlib and every project-owned
  dependency are modular. A non-modular dependency is an owner decision: port
  it first, bottom-up. Never work around it.
- **Frozen files.** Anchors and definitions are written as modules before
  approval, so frozen bytes never need a header move later. The `module` line,
  the imports, `public section` and the namespace lines belong to the frozen
  prefix. Frozen and source-facing definitions are `@[expose]`. The bundled
  `[private reference redacted].py` requires every frozen file to be a module (a
  legacy repository awaiting its port passes only with
  `--allow-non-module`). It rejects a frozen declaration or sealed export
  that the module does not export (outside `public section` and not
  `public`), and resolves `_root_.X` to `X`.
- **Worker briefs.** Repeat the module rule as a hard rule.
- **Landing checks.** Reject any tracked `.lean` file other than
  `lakefile.lean` whose first non-comment token is not `module`, and any
  `.lean` file over 10,000 lines: run the `lean-project-architecture` skill's
  `scripts/check_lean_modules.py`. Port the project's own checkers to the
  module system as well (that skill's `references/module-system.md`,
  "Checker scripts").
- **Legacy repositories.** Port a non-modular repository as its own
  campaign: mechanical pass, rebuild and repair, fresh-checkout rebuild,
  axiom and Comparator reruns, and recorded semantics-neutral hash moves for
  frozen files.

The file shape, exposure rules and porting procedure are in the
`lean-project-architecture` skill's `references/module-system.md`.

## Evidence, reporting, and landings

Treat `PROVED` as a two-key result: a prover supplies concrete evidence and a
fresh auditor tries to refute it. Report exact declarations, checks and output,
axioms, unresolved questions, draft count/paths, graph changes, and any relative
or excused-input status. Never collapse conditional and unconditional results
into one progress number.

Every campaign status report must include these explicit fields:

```text
DRAFT_ANCHORS: <count and paths>
UNREGISTERED_SORRIES: <count and paths>
DRAFT_IMPORT_VIOLATIONS: <count and paths>
SEALED_THIS_TURN: <count and exports>
```

Follow repository build and shared-checkout rules exactly. Never add custom
axioms, heartbeat overrides, unregistered placeholders, or oversized files.
Run required cache and upstream-integrity checks before Lean/Lake. Never wait,
stop, or refuse work merely because another Lean/Lake process is running;
process presence is not evidence of an upstream write. Preserve other sessions'
files and index entries; stage explicit paths, inspect the entire staged diff,
and use the repository's safe landing procedure.

## Worker brief

```text
Goal: <one bounded result>
Ownership: <files/ledger region; no other edits>
Frozen target: <ID, path, fully qualified export, pinned source/rulings>
Allowed inputs: <proved graph predecessors and approved external inputs>
Frozen files: read only; stop if the declaration appears wrong
Checks: <targeted compile, exact application, axioms, lint/ledger>
Stop condition: <precise obstruction or budget>
Hard rules: <repository-mandated text verbatim>; every .lean file is a module
  (`module` header, `public import` for the interface, `@[expose]` where
  bodies must unfold)
Handoff: files; approach; exact checks/results; axioms; uncertainty; ledger update
```

For an audit brief, require a refute-first posture, no source edits, direct
source comparison, full binder and semantic-definition classification,
exact-export compilation, and explicit statement/hypothesis/consumption/axiom
verdicts.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Account credentials are private; transcripts are shared within each CLI.
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
name=${0##*/}
case "$name" in
  <account>|<account>) ;;
  *) echo 'Invoke as <account>, <account>, <account>, <account>, <account>, <account>, <account>, or <account>.' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
family=${name%-*}
number=${name##*-}
account_dir="<accounts-dir>"
if [[ "$family" == codex ]]; then
  if [[ "$number" == 3 ]]; then
    account_dir=~/[other project redacted]
  elif [[ ! -L "$account_dir/config.toml" ]]; then
    echo "warning: $account_dir/config.toml is no longer a link to ~/[other project redacted]/config.toml; settings have diverged (see README)." >&2
  fi
  exec env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN \
    CODEX_HOME="$account_dir" /usr/bin/codex \
    -c 'cli_auth_credentials_store="file"' \
    -c 'sqlite_home="~/[other project redacted]"' "$@"
else
  # --yolo: shorthand for --dangerously-skip-permissions. Claude Code refuses
  # that flag outright for a root/sudo process unless IS_SANDBOX=1 marks it
  # as a deliberate sandbox, so --yolo sets that env var too.
  args=()
  yolo=0
  for arg in "$@"; do
    if [[ "$arg" == "--yolo" ]]; then
      yolo=1
    else
      args+=("$arg")
    fi
  done
  extra_env=()
  if [[ "$yolo" == 1 ]]; then
    args=(--dangerously-skip-permissions "${args[@]}")
    extra_env=(IS_SANDBOX=1)
  fi
  # The default profile stores global config at ~/[other project redacted], so leave

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: <accounts-dir>

# Lean project architecture

Use this skill when the main task is project design rather than one proof.
Turn the mathematical program into stable source-facing Lean declarations,
ordinary implementation modules, and a dependency graph that can be built
incrementally. Repository rules override this skill.

## The constitutional surface is actual Lean code

Select a small surface: main roots, subsection or induction gates, and
definitions whose meaning changes them. Do not freeze every helper lemma.

Only an actual final Lean declaration can be approved, manifested, frozen, or
used as a dependency-graph anchor. Markdown “contracts,” candidate APIs,
tracked probes, placeholder declarations, temporary carriers, fallback bodies,
and promises of later characterization are planning debris, not mathematics.
Pre-approval elaboration may use an untracked temporary file containing the
exact intended final command; delete it after use.

For each source-facing declaration:

1. pin the mathematical source, errata, and author rulings;
2. transcribe its premises, conclusion, quantifier order, constant/witness
   scope, and split/joint policy;
3. identify and recursively inspect every meaning-carrying carrier, definition,
   typeclass, and bundled assumption;
4. elaborate the exact final theorem type or exact final definition body;
5. obtain independent source/binder/semantics review;
6. show the complete Lean command to the author; and
7. only after approval, put one declaration in one frozen file and bind its
   source, path, fully qualified export, frozen bytes, and state in a manifest.

A topic list or source transcription is useful planning evidence but has no
declaration status. Old Lean code and old graphs are evidence to mine only
after the source-facing code is fixed.

## Freeze keystone theorem statements

An exact author-approved keystone proposition or theorem should initially have
the manifest-bound proof body `by sorry` and state `DRAFT_SORRY`. Freeze it
before graph extraction and proof assignment, rather than allowing its type to
track proof convenience. Its type, binders, imports, and meaning-carrying
definitions are already final. It is `FROZEN_UNPROVED`, not proof progress, and
production/provider modules may not import or consume it.

Allow this only in one-declaration frozen files with manifest identity, source
and declaration hashes, a named provider, and enforced quarantine. All other
`sorry`, all axioms, and every provisional definition remain forbidden.

Definition types and bodies are never provisional and neither contain nor
depend on a draft placeholder. A genuine manuscript-defined predicate may be
a literal `def : Prop`; a theorem-shaped predicate, assumption package, result
bundle, or generic “input/bridge/consequence” proposition may not replace a
theorem.

## Source-characterized definitions

A definition is acceptable only when its body already denotes the manuscript
object on its whole public carrier. Do not use an over-broad carrier plus an
`if`/`dite`/zero/default branch, choose an arbitrary non-unique witness, or
land a reconstruction whose source identity remains a future theorem.

If the source defines an object as the unique object satisfying `Φ`:

1. freeze the exact well-definedness theorem `∃! x, Φ x` as a theorem [other project redacted];
2. prove, seal, and independently audit it;
3. define the object from that proved theorem; and
4. land the definition together with a separately named, sorry-free theorem
   asserting its full source characterization and uniqueness.

The well-definedness theorem may not assume response existence, integrability,
linearity, quadraticity, representability, or another proof step unless the
source states it as a premise. Those are dependencies to prove and apply. A
Classical.choose from the proved ∃! is permitted; a fallback or non-unique
choice is not.

Treat the definition and characterization theorem as one semantic unit:
give each a manifest entry, land them in the same commit, version and audit
them together, and route every downstream graph node through
the characterization theorem rather than the raw result type. A literal source
formula or predicate may instead be defined directly after its body and carrier
have passed the same audit.

## Dependency and module architecture

1. Build the source dependency graph against exact frozen exports.
   - distinguish external black boxes, reusable infrastructure, and
     paper-specific steps;
   - make graph edges proof obligations, never added hypotheses;
   - record alternative routes explicitly instead of conjoining them;
   - review topology independently.
2. Put theorem providers below anchors in the import DAG. Providers target
   separate exports and never import drafts. Until a frozen anchor is sealed
   and audited, its registered provider module/export is itself quarantined
   from every other consumer.
3. Keep reusable infrastructure separate from paper-specific assembly.
4. Put declarations in the earliest focused module where they naturally belong.
5. Minimize imports in foundational files.
6. Search Mathlib and approved upstream APIs before inventing definitions.
7. Build APIs before downstream proofs:
   - the real definitions;
   - source characterization and basic access lemmas;
   - extensionality and simplification lemmas;
   - stable notation and coercion policy.
8. Split work into phases with stop/[other project redacted] checkpoints. Seal a theorem by changing
   only its proof body to a short `by exact Provider.result`, then run exact
   statement, axiom, and source audits.

## Lean module system (mandatory)

Every regular `.lean` file is a Lean module. This is standard from 2026-09-29.
Palomar rejects any submission containing a non-module file, and a module
cannot import a non-module file.

- **File shape.** Copyright comment; `module`; imports; module docstring;
  `public section` (or `@[expose] public section`).
- **Imports.** `public import` whatever the public interface needs; plain
  `import` for proof-only dependencies.
- **Exposure.** Definition bodies are hidden unless `@[expose]`, even from
  exported theorems in the same file. Expose source-facing, frozen and
  Challenge definitions.
- **Dependencies.** Check at planning time that every dependency is modular.
  Port bottom-up, before freezing statements when the order is still open.
- **Size.** Keep each file within 10,000 lines.
- **Checks.** Run [scripts/check_lean_modules.py](scripts/check_lean_modules.py)
  `--root <repo>` at every landing (stage new files first; it reads the git
  index) and before a release. It enforces the
  module header, the 10,000-line cap and no symlinked `.lean` files, and
  checks each `comparator.json` (modules, theorem names, standard axioms,
  NanoDa, Challenge size). Its lexer helpers are the model for a project's own
  checkers.

Read [references/module-system.md](references/module-system.md) before
writing a new repository or porting an old one, and its "Checker scripts"
section before writing or porting any script that reads Lean source.

## Statement-integrity rules

- A source-facing theorem has exactly source premises, standing assumptions,
  typing data, and explicit author rulings. Proof obligations stay in proofs.
- Expand project-owned structures and typeclasses during audit; one bundled
  argument can hide dozens of excess hypotheses.
- Audit binder order for uniform constants. An existential `C` must precede
  every parameter on which the source says it is independent.
- If one source lemma is split, require explicit author approval. Preserve a
  shared constant or witness in one joint declaration unless independent
  choices are expressly allowed.
- Conditional helpers are ordinary internal lemmas with distinct names. They
  never certify or replace the source-facing theorem.
- Frozen declarations are immutable. A defect requires an author-approved
  versioned successor and invalidates dependent [private reference redacted]audit evidence; never add
  a premise or silently substitute a helper.

## Performance and maintenance

- Keep files focused and within repository size limits.
- Prefer small helper lemmas over monolithic proofs.
- Obey repository heartbeat policy; a default-heartbeat failure is an
  architectural signal when overrides are forbidden.
- Profile before changing architecture or adding typeclass caches.
- Treat linter cleanliness and build stability as design concerns.
- Preserve other sessions' files and follow project-specific build, cache,
  staging, and landing rules.

## References

Read [references/project-architecture.md](references/project-architecture.md)
for definition engineering, file organization, Mathlib-facing conventions,
performance guidance, and cleanup expectations. Read
[references/module-system.md](references/module-system.md) for the mandatory
module-system file shape, visibility, porting, and Palomar limits.

   frozen source-facing declarations are author-approved exact Lean code; no

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per [other project redacted], until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per [other project redacted], until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-[other project redacted] with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log [other project redacted] quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr [other project redacted] to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only [other project redacted] news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell [other project redacted] before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# Proof-route survey

Date: 2026-10-06. Source locators below are local text files, with printed/PDF
pages or numbered results. Cost grades are **engineering estimates**, not
mathematical theorems or elapsed-time forecasts: A = mostly existing APIs,
B = substantial extensions, C = major new analysis, D = several new theories.
No Lean build was run. The inventory is pinned to Mathlib commit
`065356127b1dc0016f66b7283ce0ce2c4055aa55`.

## Overall routes

| Route | Mathematical inputs and source | Lean cost / risks | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1: original LT/Thomas–Fermi route | Kinetic LT; compare pair Coulomb energy with density Hartree energy plus an indirect-energy error; absorb that error with part of the kinetic energy; Thomas–Fermi molecular lower bound, Teller no-binding, atomic lower bound. `[private reference redacted]text/lieb-1990.txt`, pp. 18–20 (4.9), (4.16)–(4.19), pp. 23–25 (5.1)–(5.6); `[private reference redacted]text/lieb-1976-rmp.txt`, pp. 559–565, §§II–IV; `[private reference redacted]text/lieb-simon-1977.txt`, §V (Teller) and atomic theory. | D: nonlinear variational minimizers, Coulomb positivity, lower semicontinuity, TF Euler equations, comparison/maximum principles, screening/no-binding, plus LT. None of TF/Teller is a ready Mathlib theorem. | Keep as a literature reference and future density-functional project. Too much infrastructure for the first stability theorem. |
| R2: kinetic LT + Baxter + finite spatial cutoff | Pointwise electrostatic inequality `V≥−(2Z+1)Σ_i d_R(x_i)⁻¹`; kinetic density power; scalar Young/minimization; bound cutoff potential integral by a sum over nuclei. `[private reference redacted]text/frank-2020.txt`, pp. 7–11, Cor. 6, Thm. 7, Lem. 8; `[private reference redacted]text/lundholm-2019.txt`, pp. 102–107, Thms. 7.2–7.6. | C overall: one major electrostatics target and a manageable but nontrivial N-body Fourier/Pauli target. Final integration/algebra assembly B. | **Recommended** with explicit external-target boundaries X1–X3 and a coarser cutoff in the outline. |
| R2a: Solovej's scalar-potential/spectral presentation | Same electrostatics as R2, then spectral LT for the negative part of a truncated nearest-site one-body potential. Lundholm pp. 106–107, proof of Thm. 7.6; Frank pp. 10–11 attributes the short proof to Solovej. | If spectral LT already existed it would be short. Here it adds one-body spectral/form and fermionic [other project redacted]/variational bridges, so C–D with no benefit for our first theorem. | Regard as another presentation of the complete R2 proof, not an independent electrostatic route. Use its cutoff idea, implement the density form. |
| R3: Dyson–Lenard/local exclusion + local uncertainty | Local Pauli exclusion and uncertainty, adaptive spatial decomposition; historically a full stability proof precedes LT. `[private reference redacted]text/lieb-1990.txt`, pp. 23–25, comparison with [DL]; `[private reference redacted]text/lundholm-2019.txt`, pp. 93–98, §6.2, and pp. 106–107 assembly; `[private reference redacted]text/lundholm-solovej-2013.txt`, pp. 20–22 Lemma 6 and kinetic pressure discussion. | C–D: Sobolev/Poincaré on cubes, local particle-count probabilities, local exclusion, subdivision and tree covering. Eliminates much spectral operator theory, but not the classical electrostatic input. | Useful fallback if the direct Fourier/Pauli bridge stalls; it can still deliver kinetic LT and then use R2. |

R1 must not be summarized as simply replacing electron pair repulsion by
Hartree energy: that replacement has an error. Lieb's review explicitly
discusses it at (4.16) and again at (5.5)–(5.6). The 1975 PRL and its erratum
are not obtained; statements about the historical proof here are supported by
the obtained later accounts, not a claim to have checked its exact original
constants. The 1976 chapter is also not obtained. The Lieb–Seiringer book is
not obtained in full; chapter numbers cited by Frank/Lundholm are pointers
for author-supplied verification, not a substitute for local source evidence.

## The cutoff needed to close R2

The pointwise Baxter bound cannot be inserted into a global pointwise
minimization without a cutoff. That would involve `∫d_R^(−5/2)`; for one
nucleus its radial tail is `4π∫_1^∞r^(−1/2)dr=∞`.
**OUTLINE-ORIGINAL proof:** polar integration gives this equality and its
antiderivative `8π√r` diverges at infinity. Thus this attempted assembly
does not yield a finite bound. The source's valid argument uses
`(a/d_R−μ)_+` and subtracts μN (Frank pp. 10–11), or the same shift in
the one-body Hamiltonian (Lundholm p. 107).

The outline's variant uses `w_r=(a/d_R)1_(0<d_R<r)`, with
`a/d_R≤w_r+a/r`. It yields `∫w_r^(5/2)≤8πM a^(5/2)√r` and then
`E≥−(a/r)N−8πbκ^(−3/2)M a^(5/2)√r`, where κ is the kinetic constant.
Setting r=κ/a gives a constant times `(a²/κ)(N+M)`.
This is **OUTLINE-ORIGINAL**, with full proof at D4, L7 and T1 in
`proof-outline.md`. It avoids beta integrals and optimization in N/M.
The stronger source result involving `M^(2/3)N^(1/3)` is unnecessary for
the requested theorem (Frank p. 11). Neither version needs neutrality.

## Kinetic Lieb–Thirring routes

All routes below target the same normalized N-body inequality in dimension 3,
including spin:
`T(ψ)≥K q^(−2/3)∫ρ_ψ^(5/3)`, K universal.
Source for the spinless N-body target: Frank pp. 7–9 Corollary 6;
spin dependence: Lundholm pp. 92–93, Corollary 6.6, and Thm. 7.6.
Our explicit spin proof is at L2–L4 and is marked OUTLINE-ORIGINAL.

| Kinetic proof | Machinery actually needed | Mathlib / cost / risk |
|---|---|---|
| Original Birman–Schwinger → eigenvalue moments → Legendre duality | Self-adjoint Schrödinger form/operator, spectral resolution/min–max; compact Birman–Schwinger operators and their counting/eigenvalue bounds; integral kernels, trace estimates/ideals; resolvents and typically Fourier/Sobolev ingredients. Legendre optimization converts the `γ=1,d=3` negative-eigenvalue moment bound to the kinetic density inequality. To reach general ψ, also Pauli [other project redacted]/reduced density or a many-body variational argument. | D. Compact self-adjoint spectral theory exists, but unbounded Schrödinger spectral machinery, trace ideals and Birman–Schwinger are absent as ready APIs. Source: Frank pp. 11–15 §3, Lemma 3 p. 4 for [other project redacted]; J pp. 1–2 (1),(6),(7); original chapter unavailable. |
| Rumin through natural orbitals | Fourier on L²; low/high momentum split; Bessel inequality; Tonelli; scalar integration; one-body reduced density matrix `0≤γ≤1`, trace N, compact spectral decomposition, kinetic/density identities for [other project redacted] natural orbitals and monotone limits. No unbounded spectral theorem is intrinsic to the kinetic step. | C–D. Fourier and Bessel exist, but reduced density, infinite-dimensional traces, partial traces and kinetic trace identities need building. Source: Lundholm pp. 89–90 Thms. 6.1/6.3; Frank pp. 8–9; Rumin pp. 10–14 §3. |
| **Rumin directly on the N-body slice field** | Hilbert-valued L² Fourier; product L² regrouping and partial Fourier; rank-one coordinate projections and their algebra under swaps; low-frequency evaluation via an L² test function; reverse triangle inequality; Tonelli; a scalar power integral. No natural orbitals, partial traces, trace-class operators, min–max or unbounded spectral theorem. Hardy is used separately for the Coulomb form domain, not for kinetic LT. | **B–C, recommended kinetic implementation.** L² Hilbert-valued Fourier and rank-one maps exist. Product isometries and a.e./jointly measurable cutoff API are the largest analytic bridges. Exact argument and constant are OUTLINE-ORIGINAL at L2–L4; published antecedents are Frank p. 9 after (11), Lundholm p. 89, and J pp. 4–5 (17)–(25). |
| Lundholm–Solovej local exclusion | Local Neumann kinetic estimates/Pauli counts; Poincaré on boxes; local Sobolev/Gagliardo–Nirenberg uncertainty for density; particle-number localization; adaptive cube splitting/covering; Hölder/Jensen and finite summation. No Fourier cutoff or trace diagonalization is essential to the local argument; local min–max can sometimes be replaced by direct Poincaré and projection estimates. | C. Smooth global Sobolev infrastructure exists; local weak-H¹ estimates on cubes, exclusion/counting and adaptive covering are new. Source: Lundholm pp. 93–98 §6.2 (fermions and broader variants); Lundholm–Solovej pp. 20–22 and §§4–5. Do not claim that its anyon theorem alone proves the 3D fermion statement. |
| Frank–Hundertmark–Jex–Nam refinement | Weighted/smoothed momentum decomposition, optimized scalar profile, low-energy averaging; for dimension lifting, operator-valued LT and dimension induction. Starting formulation uses one-body density matrices. | D if implemented in full. Better constants are irrelevant to existential stability; use the simple indicator decomposition first. Source: J pp. 2–5 (8),(17)–(25), then subsequent lifting/averaging sections. |

The Rumin constant from the outline is
`K₀=(9/35)(6π²)^(2/3)=(3/7)K₃^cl`, verified by the explicit scalar integral
at L4. It is adequate; the best constant is not needed. J p. 2 (8) records
the ratio 3/7 for d=3. This is not a claim to resolve the sharp LT conjecture.

## Electrostatic proof routes and remaining cost

| Ingredient choice | Evidence / analytic machinery | Grade |
|---|---|---|
| Baxter via Voronoi boundary charge | Coulomb positive definiteness; Newton shell theorem; continuous potential excluding nearest nucleus; distributional Laplacian on polyhedral faces; positivity and energy of boundary charge; shell smearing of electrons. Lundholm pp. 102–106 Thms. 7.2,7.4,7.5 and Lem. 7.3. X3 lists precise identities and the single-/multi-nucleus split. | C–D internally; most serious risk in the whole campaign. Shell and radial integration parts are tractable. Boundary measure representation, unbounded cells and harmonic uniqueness require extra justification beyond the source's terse argument. |
| Original Baxter proof | The paper is recorded with its DOI; Project Euclid PDF retrieval failed. | Not graded against unseen details. Ask author to supply or recover official open PDF, then compare proof infrastructure before committing to the Voronoi implementation. |
| Lieb–Yau electrostatic inequality | 1988 paper, CMP 118, 177–213, deals with relativistic matter; the electrostatic ingredient is relevant independently. Full text not obtained. | No exact inequality imported from this unseen source. A stronger nearest-neighbor/positive-remainder inequality could be useful for relativistic extensions but is unnecessary here. |
| TF/indirect-energy route | Requires Coulomb energy inequalities and TF no-binding in addition to LT. Lieb 1990 pp. 18–25 and Lieb–Simon §V. | D; does not remove electrostatic infrastructure, merely changes it. |

For unequal charges, affine dependence on one charge at a time reduces to
endpoints 0,Z, then to an equal-charge subset; d_subset≥d_all keeps the
desired bound. Source: Frank p. 10 paragraph after Lemma 8; full details L6.
Do not simply replace charges by Z in the full potential: nuclear repulsion
also changes, so naive monotonicity does not prove the claim.

## Scope of the open lecture notes

Lundholm's 2019 author-posted notes provide a complete nonrelativistic stability
proof, including the electrostatic proof. They are the main implementation
source. Solovej's downloaded March 2014 *Many Body Quantum Mechanics* notes
provide Hilbert/operator/second-quantization background; that specific file
does **not** contain a complete Coulomb stability proof. Moreover the course
webpage labels 5.10 as LT, while the downloaded file labels 5.10 “Sobolev lower
bound on Schrödinger” (PDF p. 28); do not treat the webpage's numbering as a
source locator. Frank/Lundholm's attribution of the short stability proof to
Solovej is recorded without pretending it appears in that downloaded file.
The book's chapter titles and numerical constants await the full author copy.

## Recommended staging (planning only)

1. Author settles the form domain, spin and coordinate carrier, then approves
   actual exact Lean declarations; these Markdown nodes are not frozen anchors.
2. Build ordinary reusable measure/Fourier/product and smooth-core APIs (X1/X2).
3. Prove L2–L4's direct Pauli/Rumin kinetic LT, and L5's form integrability.
4. Prove the exact Baxter target X3 with an independently audited geometric
   source plan; use L6 for arbitrary bounded charges.
5. Assemble D4/L7/T1/T2, preserving the quantifier order of C(q,Z).

Every external target needs a provider before full theorem certification. No
custom axioms, unregistered sorry, heartbeat override, Lake project or build
is authorized in this phase. Proposed future modules should separate product
measure, Fourier form, Pauli, kinetic LT, classical electrostatics and assembly.

Source: F p. 7, (9) and density definition; regrouping is OUTLINE-ORIGINAL.
Dependencies: D1, X1. Lean: nonnegative marginals via `lintegral_prod` and
`AEMeasurable.lintegral_prod_right`; only convert ENNReal to real after proving
finiteness. A real Bochner integral's default value on nonintegrable functions
must never serve as the definition of an unchecked marginal.

## 4. L1 — mass, symmetry and testing the density

For every ψ∈H_N, `ρ≥0`, `ρ∈L¹`, `∫ρ=N||ψ||²`; for every measurable
`v:ℝ³→[0,∞]`,

`Σ_i ∫_(Ω_N) v(x_i)|ψ|² = ∫_(ℝ³) vρ` (extended nonnegative integrals).

For antisymmetric ψ all coordinate marginals coincide, all T_i coincide,
and `T = N T_1`; also `||F||²=N||ψ||²` and
`(2π)²∫|ξ|²||F̂(ξ)||² = T`.

Proof: Tonelli in the singled-out coordinate proves testing and mass. A swap
is measure preserving; antisymmetry cancels when taking |ψ|². It also
interchanges ξ_i and ξ_j under full Fourier transform, since the same
coordinate permutation commutes with Fourier. Summing gives the statements.
No finite-T hypothesis is needed for mass or testing. Source: F p. 7 (9),
pp. 8–9; last Fourier equalities are OUTLINE-ORIGINAL as just proved.
Dependencies: D1, D2, X1. Lean: product measure permutation and Tonelli APIs.

## 5. L2 — Pauli contraction without a density-matrix diagonalization

For every N≥1, q≥1, normalized antisymmetric ψ∈H_N and every
`f∈L²(Q;ℂ)`, define

`(B_f ψ)(z_2,…,z_N)=∫_Q overline(f(z_1))ψ(z_1,z_2,…,z_N) dz_1`.

Then `N ||B_f ψ||² ≤ ||f||²`. More generally the right side is
`||f||² ||ψ||²` for an unnormalized ψ. B_f is defined on all L² classes
by the bounded contraction on slices; Cauchy–Schwarz gives an a.e. integrable
scalar slice product and `||B_f ψ||≤||f||||ψ||`.

**OUTLINE-ORIGINAL complete proof.** For ||f||=1 let P_i be the rank-one
orthogonal projection onto f in coordinate i:
`P_iψ(z)=f(z_i)∫ overline(f(w))ψ(z_1,…,w,…,z_N)dw`.
On product functions these are commuting self-adjoint idempotent contractions.
They extend to all L² by product density and continuity. If i≠j, the image
of P_iP_j has the factor `f(z_i)f(z_j)` and is fixed by swapping i,j;
equivalently `P_iP_j U_(ij)=P_iP_j`, verified by two-coordinate Fubini on
product functions and extended by continuity. Since `U_(ij)ψ=−ψ`,
`P_iP_jψ=0`. Therefore the vectors P_iψ are orthogonal. Put
`S=Σ_i||P_iψ||²`. Self-adjointness/idempotence give
`Re⟨ψ,Σ_iP_iψ⟩=S` and orthogonality gives `||Σ_iP_iψ||²=S`.
Cauchy–Schwarz implies `S≤||ψ||√S`; S=0 is immediate, and for S>0 divide
by √S and square to obtain `S≤||ψ||²`.
Permutation symmetry gives `||P_iψ||=||P_1ψ||=||B_fψ||`, so the result
follows. For arbitrary nonzero f apply this to f/||f|| and scale B_f;
f=0 is immediate. This proof uses finite sums of bounded projections, no
compactness, spectral theorem, trace or natural orbitals.

Published comparison: F pp. 8–9 (10)–(11) proves the same Pauli bound via a
product orthonormal basis and describes the sum of rank-one projections after
(11). Our proof supplies the projection argument explicitly, including L²
extension. Dependencies: D1, X1. Lean: `InnerProductSpace.rankOne`,
`rankOne_apply`, `isIdempotentElem_rankOne_self`; lifting rank-one maps to a
chosen particle coordinate and proving the swap identities must be built.

## 6. L3 — low momentum pointwise bound

For N≥1 and normalized antisymmetric ψ, for each `E≥0`, let
`B_E={ξ∈ℝ³ : (2π)²|ξ|²≤E}`,
`F_≤E(x)=∫_(B_E) exp(2πi x·ξ) F̂(ξ)dξ`,
`F_>E(x)=F(x)−F_≤E(x)`.
The low part is a Bochner integral because its L¹ norm is at most
`|B_E|^(1/2)||F̂||₂`; it is the inverse L² transform of `1_(B_E)F̂`.
For every x its continuous representative satisfies

`||F_≤E(x)||² ≤ q |B_E| = q c E^(3/2)`, `c=1/(6π²)`.

**OUTLINE-ORIGINAL proof.** For each spin s, define g_(E,x,s) on Q by
`g(y,t)=1_(t=s) 𝓕⁻[1_(B_E)(ξ) exp(−2πi x·ξ)](y)`.
Plancherel gives `||g||²=|B_E|`. Hilbert-valued Fourier compatibility with
inner products gives `(F_≤E(x))_s = √N B_g ψ`. To verify this equality,
first use absolutely convergent products of Schwartz functions and the
Fourier inner-product identity, then extend in ψ by continuity: both maps
from H_N to L²(Q^(N−1)) have norm at most `√N |B_E|^(1/2)`.
L2 proves the squared norm of each component is ≤|B_E|. Sum over q spins.
Euclidean ball volume gives `|B_E|=(4π/3)(√E/(2π))³=cE^(3/2)`.

Choose the outer L² field F as a strongly measurable representative. The low
formula is jointly measurable in (E,x), since the cutoff condition is
measurable in (E,ξ), the phase is continuous, and parameter Bochner integrals
of this separable-valued integrand are measurable. Its norm and that of the
jointly measurable difference F_>E are measurable. No union of uncountably
many E-dependent exceptional sets is invoked.

Source basis: U p. 89, Theorem 6.1 low-energy/Bessel calculation; J pp. 4–5
(17)–(24), with the sharp indicator described after (25). Dependencies:
D2, L2, X1, X2. Lean: L² isometry, Bochner parameter integration, finite
Hilbert sum, ball volume. Missing L¹-integral/L²-inverse agreement for this
cutoff must be established by Schwartz approximation, not by assuming
the raw integral formula for every L² function.

## 7. L4 — layer-cake kinetic identity and Rumin bound

For every normalized antisymmetric form-domain ψ (N≥1),

`T = ∫_0^∞∫_(ℝ³) ||F_>E(x)||² dx dE`
`≥ K₀ q^(−2/3) ∫ρ^(5/3)`,
`K₀=(9/35)(6π²)^(2/3)>0`.

**OUTLINE-ORIGINAL proof of the N-body adaptation.** For each E, Plancherel
identifies the inner integral with
`∫ 1_((2π)²|ξ|²>E)||F̂(ξ)||²dξ`. Joint measurability from L3 and Tonelli
permit integration in E. The identity `∫_0^∞1_(E<λ)dE=λ` and L1 give T.
The reverse triangle inequality and L3 give, for a.e. x and all E,
`||F_>E(x)||≥(√ρ(x)−√(qc) E^(3/4))_+`.
For t≥0 set `E₀=(t/(qc))^(2/3)`. If t=0 both sides below vanish; otherwise
substitute E=E₀u to compute

`∫_0^∞(√t−√(qc)E^(3/4))_+²dE`
`=t E₀∫_0^1(1−u^(3/4))²du`
`=(qc)^(−2/3)t^(5/3)(1−8/7+2/5)`
`=(9/35)(qc)^(−2/3)t^(5/3)`.

Tonelli proves the inequality first as an extended nonnegative inequality;
finite T then proves `ρ^(5/3)` integrable, rather than assuming it. N=0
is immediate. Finite spin is already included in L3 and introduces exactly
q⁻²ᐟ³. For nonnormalized nonzero ψ, normalize and obtain
`T≥K₀q^(−2/3)||ψ||^(−4/3)∫ρ^(5/3)`.

Source: R §3 pp. 10–14; U p. 89 Theorem 6.1 and pp. 55–56 (4.21)–(4.24);
J p. 2 (8), which gives `K₃/K₃^cl ≥3/7`; indeed our K₀ is `(3/7)K₃^cl`.
Dependencies: L1, L3. Lean: `lintegral_prod`, nonnegative integration,
`intervalIntegral.integral_rpow`; build the scalar integral independently of
the function-space proof. This is the planned kinetic LT provider, not a
formalized theorem as of Phase 0.

## 8. X2 — Euclidean integration facts

For every r>0 and R∈ℝ³, `|B(R,r)|=(4π/3)r³` and
`∫_(|x−R|<r) |x−R|^(−5/2) dx=8π√r`; the integrand is locally integrable.
Singletons and pair-collision diagonals in product Lebesgue spaces are null.

Proof: ball volume is an existing Mathlib theorem. The radial Haar integral
formula reduces the second assertion to `4π∫_0^r t^(−1/2)dt=8π√r`.
Alternatively use layer cake: the distribution of
`1_(0<|x|<r)|x|^(−5/2)` is `(4π/3)min(r³,t^(−6/5))` for t>0;
integrating over `(0,r^(−5/2))` and `(r^(−5/2),∞)` gives
`(4π/3)√r+(20π/3)√r`. Null singletons follow from atomlessness;
Tonelli on the two singled-out coordinates proves null diagonals.

Source: U p. 107, proof of Theorem 7.6 integrates the finer cutoff; this
coarser integral and layer-cake calculation are OUTLINE-ORIGINAL as proved.
Dependencies: D1. Lean: `EuclideanSpace.volume_ball_fin_three`,
`MeasureTheory.integral_fun_norm_addHaar`, local rpow integrability and Fubini.
These facts avoid constructing spherical coordinates in the final assembly.

## 9. L5 — Hardy, Coulomb integrability and continuity of the form

For every scalar u in the Fourier H¹ form domain on ℝ³ and R∈ℝ³,
`∫ |u(x)|²/|x−R|² dx ≤4∫|∇u|²`. Consequently, for every ψ∈H_N
with finite T, every nucleus R and every distinct i,j,

`∫_(Ω_N) |ψ|²/|x_i−R| ≤2||ψ||√T_i`,
`∫_(Ω_N) |ψ|²/|x_i−x_j| ≤2||ψ||√T_i`.

**OUTLINE-ORIGINAL proof details**, consistent with U pp. 47–51,
Theorem 4.4. For C∞_c u, translate R to 0 and set
`v_ε(x)=x/(|x|²+ε²)`. Then
`div v_ε=(|x|²+3ε²)/(|x|²+ε²)² ≥|v_ε|²`.
Integration by parts has no boundary term and gives
`A_ε=∫|v_ε|²|u|² ≤∫div(v_ε)|u|²`
`=−2 Re∫ overline(u) v_ε·∇u ≤2√A_ε ||∇u||₂`.
Thus A_ε≤4||∇u||². As ε↓0, monotone convergence yields Hardy.
For general form-domain u take the X1 C∞_c core approximants. Hardy applied
to differences makes `u_n/|x−R|` Cauchy in L². An a.e. subsequence of u_n
identifies the weighted limit off {R}; norm convergence proves the same bound.
The proof works for complex u because it uses the real part.

Apply Hardy to a.e. x_i slice, treating the other positions and all spins as
parameters, and integrate using Tonelli/X1. For an electron pair, the center
is the fixed parameter x_j on that slice; the bound is uniform in this center.
Cauchy–Schwarz with |ψ| proves the two displayed Coulomb bounds. Thus every
electronic Coulomb term is absolutely integrable. Measurability follows from
the Borel distance kernel, with arbitrary finite values on the null collision
sets. No antisymmetry is needed here.

More strongly, for any such kernel k, the mixed form obeys
`|∫k overline(u)v|≤(∫k|u|²)^(1/2)(∫k|v|²)^(1/2)`.
Applied to `u=ψ_n−ψ` and `v=ψ_n+ψ`, the Coulomb expectation difference
tends to zero under H¹ convergence. Also

2. A normalized spherical shell centered at a with radius r has potential

   measure ν: on a face shared by cells k,l, density is
   `−(z/(2π)) n_k·∇|x−R_k|⁻¹`. When summing over *all* cell boundaries,
   count each face twice and use coefficient z/(4π). Prove ν has finite
   Coulomb energy and Φ=Φ_ν, including decay at infinity and uniqueness of
   the harmonic remainder. Cancellation of boundary terms and corners of
   codimension ≥2 need a polyhedral divergence theorem/approximation.
   Source U pp. 104–105 Theorem 7.5. The source treats these facts tersely;
   the formalization must supply these justifications, not add them as main
   hypotheses.
4. Complete the square:
   `D(μ,μ)−∫Φdμ+U_nuc=D(μ−ν,μ−ν)−D(ν,ν)+U_nuc`.

   A nearest face is at δ_k/2 and its exterior half-space lies in Γ_k^c;

# Author decisions before Phase 1

Date: 2026-10-06. These are recommendations, **not approved declarations or
author rulings**. None blocks the requested Phase 0 handoff. The mathematical
outline uses the defaults below consistently; changing a default requires
revisiting the corresponding statements and dependencies before freezing code.

| Decision | Options and trade-offs | Recommended default / affected nodes |
|---|---|---|
| Overall route | R1 builds TF and Teller and is historically faithful; R2 uses Baxter and a much smaller scalar assembly. R2 still has a serious classical electrostatic proof. | R2, kinetic LT + Baxter + finite cutoff; T1 and route survey. Sources: `[private reference redacted]text/frank-2020.txt` pp. 7–11 and `[private reference redacted]text/lundholm-2019.txt` pp. 102–107. |
| Kinetic proof | Natural-orbital Rumin follows published proofs closely but needs reduced-density/trace APIs; direct N-body Rumin uses rank-one projections and Hilbert-valued Fourier; local exclusion uses cubes and adaptive coverings. | Direct L2–L4 adaptation, subject to independent mathematical review before statement approval. It is OUTLINE-ORIGINAL with a complete argument, not a claim of Lean readiness. Published comparison: Frank pp. 8–9 (10)–(11), Lundholm p. 89 Thm. 6.1. |
| Electrostatic provider | Follow Lundholm's Voronoi proof; inspect the original Baxter proof for a less costly route; compare Lieb–Yau after obtaining it. | Freeze only the exact weak X3 statement after author approval; first review the proof choice, especially boundary-charge representation and finiteness. Do not import a stronger unverified inequality. |
| Role of external inputs | Prove X1/X2/X3 in the campaign; or produce a deliberately conditional assembly theorem while these are separate targets. A conditional theorem does not settle full stability. | Full target requires all providers. Allow conditional assembly only as labeled internal progress, never custom axioms or hidden hypotheses. |
| Constant quality | Existential C(q,Z); explicit coarse constant; optimize cutoff and use improved LT constants. | State existence as the source-facing [other project redacted], retain the explicit witness `max(1,8πb)(2Z+1)²/(K₀q⁻²ᐟ³)` internally. Full proof and dependence are at T1. No sharpness requirement. |
| Spin | Fixed physical q=2 reduces indexing; arbitrary finite q permits the physical theorem and quantifies degeneracy correctly. | Arbitrary q≥1, counting measure, simultaneous position-and-spin permutation. D1/L2/L3. Spin factor comparison: Lundholm p. 93 Cor. 6.8. |
| Nuclear charges | Equal charge Z only; positive integer charges; arbitrary real `0<Z_k≤Z`. | Arbitrary positive bounded real charges as requested. Endpoint argument L6 establishes the extension and does not require integer Z. Source: Frank p. 10 after Lemma 8. |
| Charge-neutrality assumption | Require N=ΣZ_k; allow arbitrary N and M. | No neutrality assumption, as in Frank Thm. 7 and T1. |

Positive coincident charges have infinite nuclear repulsion; do not use Lean's real inverse at zero. D3/T1. |

Repeated binary Tonelli/Fubini plus the finite product equivalences cover
`(ℝ³)^N`; an assembled N-body L² isometry is still project work. A product
with no coordinates has mass 1 (see `volume_pi_eq_dirac`, Pi.lean:348).

The spectral route is not impossible, but trace machinery and reduced-density
characterizations are genuinely extra targets. The direct L2 projection proof
avoids them while retaining the actual N-body state, including spin.

| Need | Search result | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Coulomb/Newton potential in ℝ³ | **absent** as a ready API | `Coulomb`, `Newton.*potential`, potential/kernel concepts and geometry/analysis filenames were searched. `Dynamics/Newton.lean` is Newton iteration, not shell electrostatics. |
| Positive definiteness of 1/|x−y| | **absent** as a ready theorem | X3 needs a convolution/Gaussian or potential proof and signed-measure integrability. |
| Newton spherical shell theorem | **absent** as a ready theorem | Polar integration exists, but the angular average and shell interaction estimates must be built. |
| Arbitrary finite nearest-site Voronoi cells | **absent** as a packaged API found | `MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers.lean` mentions Voronoi diagrams in its introductory topic list; this is not the finite-site polyhedral boundary API needed for X3. |

| Assembly's nearest-nucleus cutoff | Elementary project lemma | Finite max≤sum and translated radial integrals suffice (D4); no cell faces are needed here. |
| Lieb–Thirring, Baxter, Thomas–Fermi, Teller | **absent** as ready formalized results found | Distinct substantive targets. |

Absence means no suitable declaration was found after both filename/name
searches and concept/body searches in this pinned checkout; it is not a claim
about all future Mathlib versions. General topology, measures and convex sets
remain useful infrastructure.

## Representation recommendation and cost implications

Use bare coordinates `Fin 3 → ℝ` with explicit Euclidean length
`sqrt(Σ_a x_a²)` for product configuration bookkeeping, avoiding a deep
`EuclideanSpace` instance chain throughout N-body marginal proofs. Its standard
Pi norm is a **supremum norm**, so it must never be used silently as Coulomb
distance, momentum length, or the ball in the volume constant. Keep the
Mathlib L² Fourier/inner-product-space boundary in a small module using
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` or another explicit Euclidean wrapper, and transport
measure/pairing identities through a verified coordinate equivalence. Do not
replace physical Euclidean distances by sup distances on grounds of norm
equivalence without changing and proving every constant.

This is a Phase 0 architecture recommendation informed by the required
lean-learnings memo. No typeclass performance test was run, and no carrier
decision is frozen. Before Lean starts the author must approve exact final
declarations and their meaning-carrying definitions. Every later `.lean` file
must use the module system; current Fourier/Sobolev dependency files inspected
have `module` headers. Module compatibility of the entire eventual import
closure is a separate preflight, not certified here.

| Fubini | `MeasureTheory.integrable_prod_iff`, `MeasureTheory.integral_prod`, `MeasureTheory.integral_integral` | `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Prod.lean:230,440,468` | Bochner integrability is required. |
| A.e. slices | `MeasureTheory.Integrable.prod_left_ae`, `MeasureTheory.Integrable.prod_right_ae` | same file:245,249 | Useful for scalar Cauchy–Schwarz products. |
| Parameter Bochner integration | `MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right` | same file:67 | Joint cutoff fields after appropriate regrouping. |
| Finite product measure | `MeasureTheory.volume_pi` | `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.lean:659` | Explicitly choose volume/counting for Q; `volume` alone is not a declaration of spin counting. |
| Permuting coordinates | `MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_piCongrLeft` | same file:731 | Product measures reindexed by an equivalence. |
| Singling out coordinate | `MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove` | same file:806 | Isolates any selected `Fin (n+1)` coordinate. |
| Lebesgue under linear change | `Real.map_linearMap_volume_pi_eq_smul_volume_pi` | `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/Basic.lean:429` | Bare real coordinate products; determinant controls Jacobian. |

Repeated binary Tonelli/Fubini plus the finite product equivalences cover
`(ℝ³)^N`; an assembled N-body L² isometry is still project work. A product
with no coordinates has mass 1 (see `volume_pi_eq_dirac`, Pi.lean:348).

## Hölder, interpolation and convexity

| Need | Verified declaration | File / source line | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hölder | `ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq` | `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/MeanInequalities.lean:202` | Real conjugate exponents, nonnegative extended integrals. |
| Product membership | `MeasureTheory.MemLp.mul` | `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/CompareExp.lean:537` | `HolderTriple p q r`; use p=5/3, q=5/2, r=1. |
| Lower exponent on finite measure | `MeasureTheory.MemLp.mono_exponent` | same file:137 | Requires finite measure; cannot apply globally to Lebesgue ℝ³. |
| Finite support interpolation | `MeasureTheory.MemLp.mono_exponent_of_measure_support_ne_top` | same file:168 | Useful for a cutoff; not a substitute for global L¹ mass. |
| Finite Jensen | `ConvexOn.map_sum_le` | `Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Jensen.lean:67` | Nonnegative weights sum to 1; scalar minimization may instead use calculus. |

General Hölder is enough for the recommended assembly. No unproved global
embedding `L^(5/3)(ℝ³)⊂L¹(ℝ³)` is permitted: L1 supplies the density mass.
Integral Jensen support is available through conditional expectation
(`Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/CondJensen.lean`),
but no declaration from it is needed for this route. Exact interpolation
between L¹ mass and L⁵ᐟ³ is not consumed by the chosen coarse cutoff.

## Hilbert operators, traces and exclusion

| Need | Verified declaration / status | File / source line | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rank-one bounded operator | `InnerProductSpace.rankOne`, `InnerProductSpace.rankOne_apply` | `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/LinearMap.lean:303,322` | Bounded operator built from the inner product. |
| Norm and idempotence | `InnerProductSpace.norm_rankOne`, `InnerProductSpace.isIdempotentElem_rankOne_self` | same file:313,328 | Unit vector gives idempotence. |
| Orthogonal projections | `Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto`, `Submodule.starProjection`, `Submodule.starProjection_norm_le` | `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Basic.lean:121,132,387` | HasOrthogonalProjection hypotheses; rank-one case needs less infrastructure. |
| Bessel inequality | `Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le`, `Orthonormal.tsum_inner_products_le` | `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Orthonormal.lean:437,456` | Useful for the published orthonormal-family Rumin proof. |
| Compact self-adjoint spectral theorem | `ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_eq_bot`, `ContinuousLinearMap.finite_dimensional_eigenspace` | `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Spectrum.lean:138,463` | Exists! Orthogonal eigenspace span is dense; nonzero eigenspaces are finite dimensional. Does not itself construct the trace-class/natural-orbital API. |
| Finite-dimensional trace | `LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner`, `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.trace_eq_sum_eigenvalues` | `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Trace.lean:27,39` | The index is Fintype and/or space FiniteDimensional; **not** trace-class on L²(ℝ³). |
| Infinite-dimensional trace class / Schatten ideals | **absent** as a ready API found by this search | Filename and declaration/body searches for `TraceClass`, `trace_class`, `traceClass`, `Schatten` | `registerTraceClass` is Lean diagnostic tracing, unrelated. |
| Hilbert–Schmidt / partial traces | **absent** as a ready API found by this search | `HilbertSchmidt`, `Hilbert.Schmidt`, `partialTrace`, `partial_trace`; trace/operator filenames | Integral operator compactness and trace identities would need substantial development. |
| Unbounded self-adjoint spectral theorem | **absent** as a ready Schrödinger/Laplacian API | Spectral/compact filenames plus unbounded/spectral searches | Bounded compact spectral results must not be promoted to an unbounded spectral theorem. |
| Schrödinger min–max / Birman–Schwinger | **absent** as a ready API | `MinMax`, `min.max.principle`, `Courant.Fischer`, `Birman`, `Schwinger`; `Spectrum.lean` and `Rayleigh.lean` | `Rayleigh.lean` concerns extrema of bounded self-adjoint maps. Order `min/max` lemmas are not a min–max theorem for Coulomb Hamiltonians. |
| Permutation signs | `Equiv.Perm.sign`, `Equiv.Perm.sign_swap` | `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Perm/Sign.lean:357,388` | Suitable for product pullbacks. |
| Alternating multilinear maps | `ContinuousAlternatingMap.toContinuousMultilinearMap_injective` | `Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/Alternating/Basic.lean:62` | Exists, but arbitrary antisymmetric wave functions are not multilinear. |
| N-particle antisymmetric L² subspace, Pauli marginal bound, fermionic Fock space | **absent** as a ready API found by this search | Antisymmetry/fermion/Fock filenames and concepts | Use D1/L2; no Fock completion or trace is required for the direct projection proof. |

The spectral route is not impossible, but trace machinery and reduced-density
characterizations are genuinely extra targets. The direct L2 projection proof
avoids them while retaining the actual N-body state, including spin.

## Coulomb electrostatics and partitions

| Need | Search result | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Coulomb/Newton potential in ℝ³ | **absent** as a ready API | `Coulomb`, `Newton.*potential`, potential/kernel concepts and geometry/analysis filenames were searched. `Dynamics/Newton.lean` is Newton iteration, not shell electrostatics. |
| Positive definiteness of 1/|x−y| | **absent** as a ready theorem | X3 needs a convolution/Gaussian or potential proof and signed-measure integrability. |
| Newton spherical shell theorem | **absent** as a ready theorem | Polar integration exists, but the angular average and shell interaction estimates must be built. |
| Arbitrary finite nearest-site Voronoi cells | **absent** as a packaged API found | `MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers.lean` mentions Voronoi diagrams in its introductory topic list; this is not the finite-site polyhedral boundary API needed for X3. |
| Polyhedral face measures, boundary charge of nearest-site potential | **absent** as a ready electrostatic API | Most expensive geometric part of the Lundholm proof. |
| Assembly's nearest-nucleus cutoff | Elementary project lemma | Finite max≤sum and translated radial integrals suffice (D4); no cell faces are needed here. |
| Lieb–Thirring, Baxter, Thomas–Fermi, Teller | **absent** as ready formalized results found | Distinct substantive targets. |

Absence means no suitable declaration was found after both filename/name
searches and concept/body searches in this pinned checkout; it is not a claim
about all future Mathlib versions. General topology, measures and convex sets
remain useful infrastructure.

## Representation recommendation and cost implications

Use bare coordinates `Fin 3 → ℝ` with explicit Euclidean length
`sqrt(Σ_a x_a²)` for product configuration bookkeeping, avoiding a deep
`EuclideanSpace` instance chain throughout N-body marginal proofs. Its standard
Pi norm is a **supremum norm**, so it must never be used silently as Coulomb
distance, momentum length, or the ball in the volume constant. Keep the
Mathlib L² Fourier/inner-product-space boundary in a small module using
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` or another explicit Euclidean wrapper, and transport
measure/pairing identities through a verified coordinate equivalence. Do not
replace physical Euclidean distances by sup distances on grounds of norm
equivalence without changing and proving every constant.

This is a Phase 0 architecture recommendation informed by the required
lean-learnings memo. No typeclass performance test was run, and no carrier
decision is frozen. Before Lean starts the author must approve exact final
declarations and their meaning-carrying definitions. Every later `.lean` file
must use the module system; current Fourier/Sobolev dependency files inspected
have `module` headers. Module compatibility of the entire eventual import
closure is a separate preflight, not certified here.

   Fourier kinetic form and marginal density.

   representation, finite Coulomb energy, divergence theorem and uniqueness.

   no pointwise assumptions on arbitrary L² representatives.
3. Fourier form/H¹ equivalence, weighted smooth-core density, Hardy and
   Coulomb form integrability/continuity on the full domain.

projection/Rumin adaptation; choose the X3 proof implementation; supply the
unavailable original [private reference redacted]book if desired. Default is general q, positive

elaborated, independently audited and author-approved in a later phase.

content.text: Phase 0 is committed as `7de1b34`. Before Phase 1 (setting up the Lean project and drafting the exact Lean statements for your approval), I need a few decisions from you.

questions.question: Which overall proof route should the formalization follow?

options.label: R2: LT + Baxter (Recommended)
options.description: Kinetic Lieb–Thirring inequality, proved Rumin's way with an elementary Pauli projection argument (no trace-class operators or spectral theorem), then Baxter's electrostatic inequality V_C ≥ −(2Z+1)Σ1/d(xᵢ), then a nearest-nucleus cutoff and pointwise minimisation. This is the shortest complete route; Solovej's proof as presented by Frank and Lundholm.

options.label: R1: original LT 1975
options.description: Lieb–Thirring inequality plus Thomas–Fermi theory, Teller's no-binding theorem and an indirect-energy bound. Historically faithful, but needs nonlinear variational theory (TF minimisers, Euler equations, no-binding). Much more infrastructure.

questions.question: How should the headline stability theorem be stated in Lean?

options.label: Nonneg. extended (Recommended)
options.description: For every normalized antisymmetric ψ ∈ L²: ∫⟨attraction⟩|ψ|² ≤ T(ψ) + ∫⟨e–e repulsion⟩|ψ|² + nuclear repulsion + C(N+M), all terms in [0,∞]. Equivalent to the form bound H ≥ −C(N+M). It is trivially true when T = ∞, coincident nuclei give +∞ automatically, and no Hardy inequality or form-domain theory is needed.

options.label: Real quadratic form
options.description: Define E(ψ) = T + ∫V|ψ|² as a real number for ψ with T(ψ) < ∞, then state E(ψ) ≥ −C(N+M). Needs Hardy's inequality to show the Coulomb terms are finite, plus a separate convention for coincident nuclei. The worker's original default.

options.label: Both
options.description: The nonnegative-extended form as the frozen headline, plus a later corollary giving the real quadratic form via Hardy.

questions.question: Baxter's electrostatic inequality is the riskiest piece: the textbook proof puts charge on the boundaries of Voronoi cells and needs a divergence theorem on unbounded polyhedra, which Mathlib lacks. How should we approach it?

options.label: Research first (Recommended)
options.description: Freeze the exact Baxter statement as a gate. In parallel with the kinetic LT work, have a worker look for the most formalizable proof before committing. Candidates: a superharmonic/smoothing argument (Φ = min of superharmonic functions, avoiding polyhedral geometry) or Baxter's original 1980 proof.

options.label: Voronoi proof directly
options.description: Follow Lundholm's proof (Coulomb positivity, Newton's theorem, the Voronoi boundary measure) and build the polyhedral divergence-theorem infrastructure it needs.

options.label: Defer electrostatics
options.description: Keep Baxter as a frozen, clearly marked unproved anchor. Prove the kinetic LT inequality and the final assembly first, and revisit the electrostatics later.

questions.question: Which Lean/Mathlib base should the new project use?

options.label: Reuse [another project] pin (Recommended)
options.description: Same toolchain (v4.35.0-rc2) and Mathlib commit 0653561 that the inventory was checked against. Hard-link the already-built packages, so there's no rebuild or big download on the shared machine. Modular, with L² Fourier/Plancherel present.

options.label: Fresh latest Mathlib
options.description: Pin the newest Mathlib master and download its cache (several GB). Might have newer APIs, but the inventory would need rechecking.
